subject: Dedicated cluster sizing for HelixBiotics — sizing options and activation cadence
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alice Gomez <alice@helixbiotics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated cluster sizing for HelixBiotics — sizing options and activation cadence

Hi Alice — great meeting today, thanks for walking through the throughput and SLA expectations. As promised, attaching an initial sizing brief and a simple activation cadence workbook so your procurement and infra teams can play with the numbers. High-level options below so you can surface which direction you'd prefer for the commercial draft.

Option A — Predictable baseline (recommended for steady production):
- Minimum committed capacity: 32 GPUs (runnable lanes for isolation)
- Steady throughput target: ~120 tokens/sec sustained across primary model (Llama-variant optimized)
- Ramp: full baseline live within 2 weeks from PO + staging run for 72 hours
- Burst window: up to 64 GPUs for short bursts (pre-negotiated burst pool)
- Cost profile: lower unit cost, predictable monthly burn

Option B — Aggressive growth (early ML-heavy experiments + bursty inference):
- Minimum committed capacity: 16 GPUs with committed warm lanes, plus guaranteed burst capacity to 128 GPUs (multi-region)
- Ramp: staged 4-week activation: 16 -> 48 -> 96 -> 128 (can compress if needed)
- Cost profile: lower initial commit, higher incremental burst fees

Option C — Anchor + smoothing (balanced for unpredictable spikes):
- Minimum committed capacity: 24 GPUs anchored, autotuned smoothing for spike absorption to +40% without warm-starting new nodes
- Ramp: 3-week onramp with a 2-week staging window and 1-week performance tuning
- Additional: prefix/KV caching prewarm to reduce steady-state tokens served

Short asks for you: please confirm which option aligns with Helix’s expected 6-month burn and whether procurement wants commitment-first (A/C) or low-commit then burst (B). I included the activation workbook for you and Tom to model different ramp velocities.

Attachments: HLX_dedicated_proposal_v1.pdf (proposal + SLOs), activation-cadence-workbook.xlsx

Thanks — happy to jump on another 30m with your infra and procurement teams tomorrow afternoon (I’m flexible 1–4pm PT).

—Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com | (415) 555-0183

Subject: Re: Dedicated cluster sizing for HelixBiotics — sizing options and activation cadence

Sean — thanks, this is really helpful. A couple quick clarifying questions from our side:

1) For Option B, can you confirm whether burst to 128 GPUs would require additional region capacity (we'd prefer single-region if latency allows)?
2) For A vs C — curious whether the smoothing logic requires changes to our model serving (we're on an internal variant with 2-token response patterns that benefit from KV caching).
3) Procurement is pushing back on multi-week commitments without a clear decommit trigger. Can you provide suggested decommit windows and a credit structure for unused committed capacity?

Also looping in Tom (infra) — Tom: can you review the workbook and flag any network/egress concerns?

Thanks — Alice
Director of ML Ops | HelixBiotics
alice@helixbiotics.com

Hi Alice / Tom / procurement — answering inline: 

1) Burst locality: we can honor single-region bursting to a soft cap of 96 GPUs without cross-region fabric changes. For 128 GPUs you'll need a cross-region burst pool (adds ~8–12ms p95 tail for certain calls). If single-region is a hard constraint, recommend Option A with a larger anchor or Option C with smoothing.

2) Smoothing + serving changes: smoothing leverages our autoscaler plus prefix/KV cache warm-up. No model code changes required — we only need to ensure your model artifact supports cache warming (most Llama variants do). We'll run a 72-hour warm-run in staging to validate hit rates; engineering will provide a short checklist.

3) Decommit windows / credits: recommended decommit ladder: 30/60/90 day stepped decommit triggers. Credit structure proposal (draft):
- If decommit requested within first 30 days: 25% credit on unused committed capacity for remaining term
- 31–60 days: 50% credit tapering to 75% after 60 days (examples in attached workbook)
- Beyond 90 days: standard termination (pro-rated final month, no credit)

I've attached a short appendix in the proposal with sample financials for each option and the credit examples. Karthik — can you add a line item for SLA exception pricing if Helix requires a stricter p99 target?

Next steps: Tom and procurement — if you can mark which option you'd prefer and send any redlines on the credit structure, I'll turn this into a formal commercial draft and route to legal. Happy to host a 30m war room for PO + legal signoff.

—Sean

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated cluster sizing for HelixBiotics — sizing options and activation cadence

Sean — quick internal note: for the SLA exception pricing, suggest we model p99 at two tiers: 300ms (standard) and 180ms (premium). Put the premium as an uplift on Option A (~+18% commitment fee) and on burst fees for B/C as a separate add-on. Also call out the warm-cache credits as a one-time onboarding credit rather than a recurring discount — keeps renewal math cleaner.

Monica — can you own the activation workbook updates (timeline + credits) and validate the 72-hour warm-run assumptions? I can take the SLA pricing into the commercial draft.

Thanks — Karthik
Head of Solutions | Redwood Inference
